body: **Foco:** Reporting verbs — produção e revisão.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (B2):** eu consigo produzir um relato oral com vários verbos de relato a partir de um texto acadêmico e usar sort out.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Public Trust in Science: Survey Findings
paras: The researchers **report** that trust in scientists remains high. Respondents **said** that scientists act in the public interest, although many **admitted** that they find research hard to follow. The authors **argue** that clearer communication could **sort out** much of the confusion.
Critics **point out** that surveys can **overstate** trust. The team **denied** ignoring this limitation and **recommended** repeating the survey yearly.

items.q: Respondents said research is easy to follow.
The team recommended repeating the survey yearly.

blocks.cap: Verbos de relato em textos acadêmicos

blocks.body: Em textos acadêmicos, escolha o verbo conforme a **força do argumento**: *note* (neutro), *argue* (defende), *claim* (reivindica, com cautela), *demonstrate* (prova).

items.s: The researchers ___ that trust remains high. (report)
The authors ___ that clearer communication could help. (argue)
The team ___ ignoring this limitation. (deny, past)
Clearer talk could ___ out the confusion. (sort)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Go on record.** — Declarar oficialmente.
**Speak for itself.** — Falar por si.
**Beyond doubt.** — Fora de dúvida.
**On balance.** — No geral.
**Take stock.** — Fazer um balanço.
**Come to terms with.** — Aceitar.
**What did the researchers report?** — O que os pesquisadores relataram?
**That trust in scientists remains high.** — Que a confiança nos cientistas continua alta.
**What did critics point out?** — O que os críticos apontaram?

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence summary of the text using six different reporting verbs.
blocks.model: The researchers report that trust in scientists remains high. Respondents said that scientists act in the public interest. Many admitted that research is hard to follow. The authors argue that clearer communication could help. Critics point out that surveys can overstate trust. The team recommended repeating the survey yearly.
